assessment.nobel_worthiness: Predicting the Z2 topological insulator and the quantum spin Hall effect, then observing edge transport in HgTe quantum wells, opened a field of topological band theory. The idea is original, conceptually clear, and has spread across condensed matter, photonics and materials science. It is one of the strongest cases on the list for lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the decisive theoretical proposal (Z2 classification, graphene model). Molenkamp's group made the experimental realization in HgTe/CdTe following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal, and that proposal is not among the credited names here. Hasan's 3D work and the BHZ theory are real parts of the story, so a three-person split omits legitimate contributors.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally confirmed by several independent groups and materials for more than fifteen years, and the interpretation is stable. Recognition is timely and no longer early.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should centre on 2D quantum spin Hall or on 3D topological insulators, and who is left out in either case.
Overlap with candidates B016 and B048-type topological entries; my recollection of the exact priority chronology is not independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: IceCube opened neutrino astronomy by detecting a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos, evidence for TXS 0506+056 as a source and later Galactic-plane neutrinos. It is a major instrumental achievement and a new observational window. Its significance is at the level of a prize in astroparticle physics.
assessment.attribution: Halzen is the only credited name and was the long-standing scientific leader and driving force of IceCube. Neutrino astronomy rests on a large collaboration and on earlier pioneering efforts (DUMAND, AMANDA, and others). A single-laureate prize would understate that history, but only the one credited name is available to me.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is well established. Source identification is still limited to a few objects, and the origin of most of the flux remains unresolved. This is mature as an instrument and a discovery, but the astrophysics is still being filled in.
uncertainties: Whether the credit list is too narrow for a fair configuration.
The significance of the source associations is still developing.
I work in the neighbouring field of astroparticle physics and should rely on the evidence rather than familiarity.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum simulation of strongly correlated matter with ultracold atoms in optical lattices (the Hubbard-model proposal, the superfluid to Mott insulator transition, and single-site-resolved microscopy) created a controllable platform for many-body physics. The originality and the lasting influence on condensed matter and quantum information are high.
assessment.attribution: Zoller and Cirac (with Jaksch) supplied the key theory for cold atoms in lattices, and Bloch, Greiner and Esslinger carried out the decisive experiments. Choosing among Greiner, Esslinger and Bloch is a hard allocation question, and Greiner's and Esslinger's contributions are substantial. I propose a theory-plus-experiment pairing, which is only one of several defensible splits.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed in many labs for twenty years, with analog quantum simulation now widely used. Recognition is timely, though practical quantum advantage is still being established.
uncertainties: Allocation among Bloch, Greiner and Esslinger is unresolved.
Overlap in names with B006 and B040 may complicate a multi-candidate comparison.
How far the claim of impact on real strongly correlated materials is realized is still debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The BeppoSAX X-ray afterglow detection and the subsequent optical identification and redshift measurements settled the cosmological origin of gamma-ray bursts. This ended a decades-long debate and led to the use of bursts as probes of the early Universe. It is a clear, decisive observational discovery.
assessment.attribution: Costa and Frontera led the BeppoSAX discovery of the X-ray afterglow, while the optical and redshift confirmation involved teams around van Paradijs, Djorgovski, Metzger and Kulkarni. Jan van Paradijs (deceased) cannot be credited, and the optical credit is shared among several groups, so attribution is truly disputed.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by thousands of subsequent bursts across missions (Swift, Fermi) and now well established. It is mature and, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: Distribution of credit between the X-ray and optical discoveries.
Whether three names can fairly cover a compound discovery.
My own interest in gamma-ray instrumentation is a reason to weigh this by the evidence only.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction of flat bands at the magic angle and the experimental discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene created the field of moire quantum matter. It is original, clear and has led to rapid follow-on discoveries such as fractional Chern insulators.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the flat bands, and Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive transport discovery. Others, such as Dean, Young and Yazdani on related experiments, and Kim and Efetov on parallel work, are not credited, so the list is incomplete for the full field.
assessment.maturity: The phenomena have been reproduced widely, though the mechanism of superconductivity remains debated and the field is only about eight years old. This is somewhat early for a prize.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism in magic-angle superconductivity is unresolved.
Possible premature recognition compared with the older candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and developed by Ye to reach the 10^-18 level, enables precision tests of fundamental physics, relativistic geodesy and a prospective redefinition of the second. The importance for metrology is high and the work is clear and well characterised.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept, and Ye's group achieved the leading precision. Hall and Hansch were already honoured in 2005 for the comb and the Ye link is partly through that work. Contributions from Ludlow, Derevianko, Lemonde and others are significant but not credited. Two names give a clean configuration.
assessment.maturity: Independent clocks at several institutes agree at the 10^-18 level, and the redefinition of the second is under discussion. This is mature but the practical applications are still emerging.
uncertainties: Whether the prize would be seen as an extension of previous clock and comb awards.
Redefinition timeline of the second is not settled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical detection and coherent control of single nitrogen-vacancy centres in diamond turned a defect into a room-temperature qubit and nanoscale sensor, with applications from quantum networks to biology. The discovery is original and has a broad influence on quantum sensing.
assessment.attribution: Wrachtrup and Jelezko demonstrated the single-NV detection and control, and Lukin's group developed the sensing and quantum register ideas. Others (Awschalom, Hanson, Yacoby, Budker and more) made major contributions, and B001 also credits Wrachtrup, so overlap exists.
assessment.maturity: The results are reproduced widely, and many applications are available commercially. Recognition is timely, but the technology's long-term impact remains partly prospective.
uncertainties: Credit overlap with other solid-state spin candidates.
Which of sensing or qubit work should be the central achievement.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The ATLAS and CMS experiments discovered the Higgs boson and completed the Standard Model's particle content. The detector conception and construction were extraordinary experimental achievements. The theory was recognised in 2013, but experimental recognition remains outstanding.
assessment.attribution: The discovery is the work of several thousand collaborators. The three credited names were founding leaders of the proposals, which is a defensible but contestable proxy for a collective achievement. Spokespersons at the time of discovery and key detector and analysis leaders are not credited.
assessment.maturity: The Higgs boson is firmly established and its couplings have been measured for more than a decade. Timing is not an issue, but the attribution question is hard.
uncertainties: The Nobel statutes make recognizing a collaboration difficult.
Whether founding proposers or discovery-era leaders are the right laureates.
I have collaboration experience and should avoid overweighting instrumental work.
